clue.text: Present record about time of some of our peers?

parts.note: present means in attendance, here

indicators.note: the record goes around the time letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: A question about how long a present-day record of our nobility has been kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside DIARY, after HERE. Some British peers sit in the House of Lords by birthright rather than appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Some members of the British peerage hold their titles by inheritance, passed down from parent to child.

clue.text: Tramp gives house unpleasant smell

parts.note: BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A vagrant leaves a home stinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter who wanders without home or work, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Pole gathers up article in street

indicators.note: the pole collects the article within itself, holding it inside

parts.note: a rod is a pole
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A man from Poland collects an item in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathers up' puts A inside ROD. 'Pole' is capitalised to suggest a Polish person; it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thoroughfare for traffic in a town.

clue.text: Desirable age to become stroppy

indicators.note: the letters of the two words turn into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Reaching a sought-after age makes someone grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' shuffles DESIRABLE and AGE together. 'Stroppy' is British slang for bad-tempered and difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe a person who is bad-tempered and hard to get along with.

clue.text: Woman's attempt to conceal account

indicators.note: the attempt hides the account inside itself

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A woman tries to cover up some bookkeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' puts AC inside TRY; the 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a woman can be called by it.

clue.text: Socialist island, French and a source of food

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or socialist
Mull is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A left-wing islander and a Frenchman share a source of nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish caught and eaten, prized as a seafood dish.

clue.text: Trainee pixie lacking resolve

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
an imp is a small mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A novice fairy who is feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy and without firmness, figuratively weak in will.

clue.text: To the extent that disruption's affected Asian chums?

indicators.note: the friends' letters are disturbed and thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking how far a group of Asian friends has been upset by some disruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption's affected' rearranges the letters of ASIAN CHUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal conjunction meaning in so far as, or because.

clue.text: Windows, perhaps, on Mediterranean, according to plan?

parts.note: Microsoft Windows is an example of a computer program
MED is a short name for the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Wondering whether holiday windows overlooking the Mediterranean were part of the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places MED after PROGRAM, as in a down clue one piece sits on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set up in advance is scheduled or planned out.

clue.text: These players will have a bit of cheek?

definitions.text: These players will have a bit of cheek?

parts.words: These players will have a bit of cheek?
parts.note: cheek means impudence, also called brass, and groups of musicians are bands; such musicians also puff out their cheeks

explanation.surface: A suggestion that some sportsmen will be cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensembles of trumpets, horns and tubas, players who blow with puffed-out cheeks.

clue.text: Mexican meal old jazz fan knocked back

indicators.note: back signals the combined letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: An elderly jazz lover downs a Mexican dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns O + CAT round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded tortilla with a filling, a staple dish of Mexico.

clue.text: Possibly the negative picture of racial distribution

indicators.note: the word could be arranged otherwise, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: no is a negative answer
a graphic is a picture or illustration

explanation.surface: Perhaps a photographic negative showing how races are spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges THE into ETH; 'negative picture' looks like photography but splits into NO and GRAPHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the description of peoples and their cultures and where they live.

clue.text: Ill-favoured type whose always right, one hard to deal with?

parts.note: ill-favoured means unattractive, ugly
the shop saying goes that the customer is always right

explanation.surface: A plain-looking shopper who insists on being right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whose' stands for 'who's' as printed. The phrase is an idiom for an awkward, threatening person.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an unpleasant, potentially violent or difficult person.

clue.text: Sudden decline of Aire's carp mentioned

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A fish from the Yorkshire river Aire is mentioned in connection with a sudden fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England. The letters span AIRE'S CARP MENTIONED.
explanation.definitionFit: A long steep slope or cliff, where land drops abruptly.

clue.text: Recent changes taking turn in charge of number 1?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the turn, holding it inside
the word is altered into a different arrangement

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Recent changes give a turn to whoever is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges RECENT into ECENTR; 'taking' puts GO after its E; IC follows. 'Number 1' means oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred, thinking only of oneself, the person who looks after 'number one'.

clue.text: Say people must be housed in cowshed, mostly in sections

indicators.note: the people are lodged inside the shed
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a stall is a compartment for a cow in a shed
EG, for example, means say
men are people

explanation.surface: People must be put up in a barn, mostly in separate parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts STALL to STAL; 'housed in' puts EG and MEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Divided into segments or parts.

clue.text: Attempt to eat chip and reportedly get on drug

indicators.note: the attempt swallows the chip, holding it inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
IC is an integrated circuit, a computer chip

indicators.note: the next piece is given by how a word sounds

parts.note: to click is to get on well with someone

explanation.surface: Trying to eat chips and then take some medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts IC inside TRY; 'reportedly' gives CLIC, sounding like CLICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A class of antidepressant medicines named for their three-ring molecular structure.

clue.text: find a sound system

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'find a sound system (5)' is cut short from OCR; no wordplay for NICAM survives and no source gives the full text.

clue.text: Capital account sent to artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Money in an account is sent on to a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent to' places RA after ACC.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: Make one odd shape of granite to note

indicators.note: the stone is given a strange new form, its letters rearranged

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions to carve a strange shape from granite and attach a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd shape of' rearranges GRANITE into INTEGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine parts into a single whole.

clue.text: Pleasant year spent in danger spots?

indicators.note: the words are used up and come out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A nice twelve months spent in risky places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' rearranges PLEASANT YEAR. In football, the box in front of goal is the dangerous zone where fouls give penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: The marked boxes in football where a foul gives a penalty kick and goals threaten.

clue.text: It's said to come down as a rule

indicators.note: the next word is given by its sound when spoken

parts.note: rain is what comes down from clouds

explanation.surface: A remark that something generally falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a' is a link; the surface leans on the phrase 'as a rule'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to govern as monarch.

clue.text: Opera singer is keen to come up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: avid means keen

explanation.surface: A soprano is eager to get on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated female lead vocalist in opera.

clue.text: Smile in support

definitions.meaning: a horizontal timber or girder that holds things up

explanation.definitionFit: Grinning widely; also a structural joist bearing a load.

clue.text: River's tidal bore?

indicators.note: tides churn and shift water about, so the word's letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A tidal wave on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore is a tidal wave up a river, but here 'tidal' signals that the letters of BORE are churned into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A major river of north-east Spain.

clue.text: Journey made by team round town with river

indicators.note: the team goes around the town and river

parts.note: a side is a team
Leigh is a town in Greater Manchester, England

explanation.surface: A trip taken by a group around a riverside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' places LEIGH and R inside SIDE. The team in the definition sense is a team of reindeer or horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip in a horse-drawn or reindeer-drawn sled over snow.

clue.text: Friar having adjustment to make garment smaller?

definitions.meaning: a fold sewn into clothing to take it in

explanation.definitionFit: The jovial monk of Robin Hood legend; also a stitched fold that shortens or narrows clothing.

clue.text: Breaking images could give mason colic

indicators.note: the letters could produce a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A stonemason suffering stomach pains from smashing statues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could give' rearranges MASON COLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The destruction of religious images, or attacking cherished beliefs.
